message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look list of the long weekends that Canadians can take advantage of in 2023.  
(Only the holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday – or are observed on the nearest Monday if they fall on a weekend – are shown.)

| Long‑Weekend | Holiday(s) | Dates (2023) | Notes |
|--------------|------------|--------------|-------|
| **Family Day** (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Ontario) | Family Day | **Feb 20** (Mon) | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **Feb 17 – Feb 20** |
| **Good Friday** (most provinces) | Good Friday | **Apr 7** (Fri) | Creates a 3‑day stretch: **Apr 7 – Apr 9** |
| **Victoria Day** (all provinces) | Victoria Day | **May 22** (Mon) | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **May 19 – May 22** |
| **Canada Day** (federal employees & some provinces) | Canada Day | **Jul 3** (Mon) – observed because Jul 1 fell on Saturday | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **Jul 1 – Jul 3** |
| **Labour Day** (all provinces) | Labour Day | **Sep 4** (Mon) | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **Sep 1 – Sep 4** |
| **Thanksgiving** (all provinces) | Thanksgiving | **Oct 9** (Mon) | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **Oct 6 – Oct 9** |
| **Christmas Day** (all provinces) | Christmas Day | **Dec 25** (Mon) | Creates a 4‑day stretch: **Dec 22 – Dec 25** |

### Quick Summary

- **Feb 17‑20** – Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Ontario)  
- **Apr 7‑9** – Good Friday (most provinces)  
- **May 19‑22** – Victoria Day (all provinces)  
- **Jul 1‑3** – Canada Day (observed on Monday for federal employees; some provinces observe on Monday)  
- **Sep 1‑4** – Labour Day (all provinces)  
- **Oct 6‑9** – Thanksgiving (all provinces)  
- **Dec 22‑25** – Christmas Day (all provinces)  

*(New Year’s Day fell on Sunday, and Remembrance Day fell on Saturday, so they didn’t create extra long weekends.)*  

Feel free to plug these date ranges into your holiday‑planning app!
